items.title: Gardes à vue allongées, aides sociales ponctionnées et couvre-feu à Marseille : l’exécutif tente de reprendre la main
items.description: Face aux scenes de pillages et d'affrontements qui ont secoue plusieurs villes , le gouvernement multiplie les annonces pour reprendre le controle. Le ministre de la Justice ouvre la voie a des gardes a vue plus longues, celui de la Ville et du Logement cible le portefeuille des delinquants et celui de l'Interieur resserre le dispositif sur le terrain, notamment a Marseille. Des outils judiciaires renforces et un signal economique fort Invite du 20 heures de TF1, le 19 octobre, le ministre de la Justice Gerald Darmanin a annonce avoir adresse « une instruction a tous les parquets de France pour leur demander de passer en qualification de criminalite organisee ». La requalification permet de faire passer les gardes a vue de 48 a 72 heures, d'autoriser les geolocalisations et les ecoutes telephoniques, et de recourir a la reconnaissance faciale en croisant les images des reseaux sociaux avec le fichier de traitement d'antecedents judiciaires. J’ai envoyé ce matin une instruction à tous les parquets de France pour leur demander de retenir les qualifications de criminalité organisée face à ces actes extrêmement graves. Sous ce régime, les gardes à vue pourront être prolongées jusqu’à 72 heures, des géolocalisations et des écoutes téléphoniques seront possibles et, pour la première fois dans ce contexte, nous aurons recours à la reconnaissance faciale pour identifier ceux qui revendiquent des violences et des pillages, notamment sur les réseaux sociaux. — Gérald DARMANIN (@GDarmanin) October 19, 2026 Au total, 2 513 gardes a vue ont ete recensees depuis samedi, selon lui, et pres des deux tiers se poursuivaient lundi soir. Le meme soir, 67 personnes etaient deja incarcerees, un chiffre porte ensuite a 123. Parallelement, le ministre de la Ville et du Logement Vincent Jeanbrun a annonce une circulaire commune avec Gerald Darmanin visant a reduire les aides sociales des pilleurs. « Casseurs, pilleurs, voleurs : les prestations sociales, c'est termine ! Nous prenons une circulaire avec [Gerald Darmanin] pour que les delinquants se voient retirer de leurs prestations sociales l'equivalent des sommes issues de leurs trafics ou recel », a-t-il ecrit sur X. Casseurs, pilleurs, voleurs : les prestations sociales, c’est terminé ! Nous prenons une circulaire avec @GDarmanin pour que les délinquants se voient retirer de leurs prestations sociales l’équivalent des sommes issues de leurs trafics ou recel. 👇 https://t.co/49FNCt1tpU — Vincent Jeanbrun (@VincentJeanbrun) October 19, 2026 Les revenus tires de la revente de biens voles seront integres au calcul du revenu de solidarite active, des allocations chomage, des aides au logement et des allocations familiales. La mesure, qui s'etend a d'autres formes d'economie souterraine, complete le futur projet de loi « casseur-payeur ». Laurent Nuñez a promis un dispositif policier « tres important » pour la mobilisation de samedi et justifie les couvre-feux. Un couvre-feu pour les mineurs, de 22 heures a 5 heures, s'applique de mardi a vendredi dans certaines zones de la ville et de communes des Bouches-du-Rhone . Ces mesures ciblees, deja en vigueur dans d'autres agglomerations, doivent permettre de contenir de nouveaux debordements tout en affichant la fermete de l'executif.

items.title: Conférence de l’ONU sur l’eau 2026 : Le Sénégal veut mobiliser 2 631 milliards de FCFA
items.description: Le Sénégal ambitionne de mobiliser 4,5 milliards de dollars, environ 2 631 milliards de FCfa pour renforcer la sécurité de l’eau et de l’assainissement. L’annonce a été faite ce mardi 20 octobre à Dakar par le ministre de l’Hydraulique et de l’Assainissement, Cheikh Tidiane Dièye, à l’ouverture de l’atelier national préparatoire à la Conférence des Nations Unies sur l’eau, prévue du 8 au 10 décembre 2026 à Abu Dhabi, aux Émirats arabes unis. Cette enveloppe correspond au Compact national pour la sécurité de l’eau, évalué à 4,5 milliards de dollars. Pour le ministre, l’enjeu est désormais de passer des engagements aux réalisations concrètes. « La question clé étant de savoir comment convertir les engagements en investissements, les priorités en réalisations concrètes », a-t-il déclaré. Le Sénégal entend profiter de cette conférence, qu’il coorganise avec les Émirats arabes unis, pour renforcer son positionnement international et porter les priorités africaines en matière de gouvernance de l’eau. « Nous sommes là pour construire la voix du Sénégal, celle qui portera, à Abu Dhabi, les aspirations de notre pays, les priorités de l’Afrique », a souligné Cheikh Tidiane Dièye. Le ministre a également annoncé le lancement prochain du Pacte présidentiel sur l’Eau par le chef de l’État, Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye, dans le cadre de l’Agenda Sénégal 2050. Il a appelé à une mobilisation collective pour faire de la conférence un levier de financement et d’amélioration des services d’eau et d’assainissement. Babacar Guèye DIOP

items.title: Vision FC: Coach Jaredic resigns after one win in eight
items.description: Montenegrin coach Predrag Jaredic has resigned from his position as head coach of Vision F.C, the club has announced. A club statement on Tuesday morning said “Vision Football Club confirms that Predrag Jaredic has resigned from his position as Head Coach with immediate effect.” Jared won one out of eight Ghana Premier League matches – the opening day victory over Young Apostles on September 5. Since then, Vision has lost three league matches, including consecutive defeats in the last two, and three draws. Jaredic’s last league match was a 0-1 home defeat to Accra Hearts of Oak on Saturday. “We thank him for his service to the club and wish him the very best in his future endeavours”, the club statement added. items.title: GoldBod reforms create 4,866 direct jobs in less than two years – Sammy Gyamfi
items.description: The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) says its institutional, licensing and value addition reforms have created 4,866 direct jobs in less than two years, as Ghana seeks to expand local participation in the gold industry. Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi said the jobs comprised 361 public-sector positions and 4,505 private-sector jobs. He added that the reforms were creating further opportunities across the gold value chain for artisanal smelters, jewellers and young entrepreneurs. Speaking at the African Minerals Policy Forum – Mining in Motion 2026, Mr Gyamfi stressed that African countries must build mineral economies that generate decent jobs and opportunities for their citizens while protecting the environment. He said the success of the sector should be measured not only by production volumes but also by the economic and social benefits retained by local communities. “Support for private enterprise and job creation in the mineral and mining economy, must therefore be a priority for all African nations,” he said. Mr Gyamfi further argued that mineral sovereignty must create pathways for Africans to become mine owners, geologists, engineers, equipment providers, financiers, processors, refiners and traders, rather than being confined to low-value activities in the mining chain.

items.title: Du braquage aux incantations, un guérisseur cueilli par la Police
items.description: Recherché pour des faits présumés de cambriolages, de vols à main armée et d’association de malfaiteurs, un ancien détenu reconverti en guérisseur traditionnel a été interpellé au marché de Djékpétimey, à Djakotomey, au Bénin. Une perquisition à son domicile a permis de découvrir notamment des marteaux, une machette et une plaque d’immatriculation de motocyclette, selon la Police républicaine, qui a rendu l’information publique ce mardi 20 octobre 2026. Le passé a fini par rattraper celui qui semblait avoir tourné la page de ses anciennes activités. Après un séjour en prison, cet homme, recherché pour des faits présumés de cambriolages, de vols à main armée et d’association de malfaiteurs, s’était reconverti dans la médecine traditionnelle. Installé dans le village de Gbégnadji, dans l’arrondissement d’Adjido, commune de Toviklin, il y recevait ses patients et leur prodiguait des soins. Mais cette reconversion n’a pas mis fin aux soupçons qui pesaient sur lui. Déjà cité dans une affaire de braquage dont les complices présumés sont détenus à la maison d’arrêt de Lokossa, il aurait, de nouveau, été impliqué dans plusieurs cambriolages et braquages, selon les informations rapportées dans cette affaire. Face à ces nouveaux soupçons, les enquêteurs ont mis en place une filature discrète. Au terme de leurs investigations, les policiers ont finalement localisé et interpellé le suspect au marché de Djékpétimey, à Djakotomey, mettant ainsi fin à sa cavale. La perquisition menée à son domicile a permis de découvrir plusieurs objets, dont des marteaux, une machette et une plaque d’immatriculation de motocyclette. Ces éléments devront être examinés dans le cadre des investigations destinées à établir les circonstances des faits qui lui sont reprochés. Du statut de repris de justice à celui de guérisseur traditionnel, l’homme semblait avoir changé de voie. Mais les nouveaux soupçons ont fini par remettre son passé au centre de l’attention des enquêteurs. Son interpellation marque une nouvelle étape dans cette affaire, sans toutefois préjuger de sa culpabilité. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Du braquage aux incantations, un guérisseur cueilli par la Police est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: CCC to honour teachers as part of its October Commission, offers free medical screening to hundreds
items.description: The Calvary Charismatic Centre (CCC) has announced plans to honour teachers in the Ashanti region for their immense and selfless contribution to education and national development. The recognition is part of activities marking the church’s annual October Commission. The church has scheduled November 1 for a Teachers Honouring Sunday to recognise the role of teachers in shaping future generations. Resident Pastor of CCC at Ayigya, Joshua Obeng, described teachers as the “heart and soul of a nation,” emphasising the need to recognise their contribution to society and encourage them to continue delivering quality education. “Everyone was trained by a teacher, and so if we can honour them so that they at least feel their importance and the need to continue to teach the students well, then we know that certainly we’ve done something that will go ahead and be an influence to generations to come,” he said. Pastor Obeng explained that the planned event forms part of the church’s broader commitment to community engagement through its October Commission, an annual initiative aimed at spreading the gospel and demonstrating the love of God through practical support. As part of this year’s activities, the church organised a free medical and dental outreach on Saturday, October 17, at CCC Agape City at Ejisu-Krapa in the Ashanti Region. The exercise offered residents free medical screening, including blood pressure and blood sugar checks, as well as dental screening and consultations. It also formed part of the church’s efforts to address health needs and promote awareness of preventive healthcare in surrounding communities. Pastor Obeng said the October Commission provides an opportunity for the church to reach beyond its congregation and extend support to people in need. “October Commission is always a time when we use to spread the love of God to our communities,” he said. He noted that the church’s activities during the period also include the distribution of clothes, foodstuff, and other essential items to support beneficiaries. “One of the things we do during that time is to do a medical outreach and free giveaway of clothes, of foodstuff, and other things, as sharing our love to the various communities,” he added. According to him, Ejisu-Krapa was selected for this year’s outreach to enable the church to share its resources with residents and bring them hope and encouragement. “This year we decided to come to Ejisu-Krapa to set up here to show the Ejisu-Krapa community our love and to bring hope and joy into the heart,” he said. He expressed satisfaction with the response from residents and prayed for the strength and resources to extend greater support to communities during future editions of the initiative. Beyond the medical outreach and the planned recognition of teachers, CCC also intends to extend its evangelism activities to Adum as part of efforts to spread the gospel and encourage residents. The activities form part of the church’s wider October Commission programme, which combines evangelism with community service and initiatives aimed at recognising the contributions of individuals who play important roles in society.

items.title: Sindh cabinet decides to make judicial commission's report on Mir Raza murder case public
items.description: KARACHI: The Sindh cabinet on Tuesday decided to make the report prepared by a judicial commission formed to investigate the circumstances and possible negligence in businessman Mir Raza Ali’s murder investigation public. According to a handout issued by the Sindh chief minister’s spokesperson, the decision was taken during a meeting chaired by CM Murad Ali Shah. The statement said the judicial inquiry report, which was presented in seven separate sealed envelopes, will be uploaded on the website of the provincial home department on Tuesday, while a copy will also be provided to the aggrieved family. Further, CM Shah also constituted a four-member sub-committee to ensure the implementation of the report. The committee comprises Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar, Local Government Minister Nasir Hussain Shah, Labour Minister Saeed Ghani and the Sindh advocate general. Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon also took to X to announce that the report would be made public on Tuesday. “The government of Sindh remains committed to transparency, accountability and ensuring that due process of law is upheld,” he said. Last week, the commission, headed by Justice Omar Sial of the Sindh High Court (SHC), had handed over the sealed report to the provincial government after examining 49 witnesses during 15 hearings. The inquiry report along with associated documents was handed over to focal person of the provincial government and additional secretary of home department Javed Ahmed Abro by registrar of the commission Abdul Majid on the premises of the SHC. After receiving the record, Abro told reporters that he would hand over the sealed report along with other record to the provincial government and it was the prerogative of the government to decide whether the inquiry report was to be brought into the public domain or otherwise. In August the provincial government formed the commission, which was tasked with making recommendations for further investigation and forensic analysis or legal/departmental action and it was required to submit its findings and recommendations to the Sindh government within 30 days. However, the commission had struggled to meet its deadline and sent an application last month to the Sindh government for an extension in its tenure till Oct 15. Therefore, the provincial cabinet granted an extension. Besides examining 49 witnesses and available record, the commission had also sent questionnaires to Karachi police chief Azad Khan, head of current investigation team DIG Amir Farooqui and DIG East Farrukh Lanjar after dismissing an application of aggrieved family to summon the senior police officers to testify before the commission. The 25-year-old businessman and Institute of Business Administration graduate had gone missing on July 28 after leaving his home in PECHS and his body with gunshot wounds was found a day later in bushes in a Gulistan-i-Jauhar’s locality. Initially, the police built the case around suicide on the basis of the first autopsy , which indicated a bullet entry wound on the chest, and by pointing out business losses and money borrowed by the victim. Police surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed had disputed the findings of the first post-mortem conducted by medico-legal officer Dr Osama Sheikh. The second post-mortem report, however, termed its findings “inconsistent” with suicide as the manner of Mir Raza’s death. It said the Exhumation Board was of the unanimous opinion that the death was caused by a gunshot wound to the back.

items.title: Gunmen kill NSCDC officer, abduct businessman in Plateau
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa Gunmen have reportedly killed a serving officer of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, NSCDC, and abducted a businessman in Pushit community, Mangu Local Government Area of Plateau State. The incident occurred at about 9:30 p.m. on Monday, despite a dusk-to-dawn curfew recently imposed in parts of the area following repeated attacks. A member of the community, Lawrence Tabitha, told newsmen that “the deceased, a Deputy Superintendent of the NSCDC, was shot near his residence while riding his motorcycle.” Tabitha said, “The gunmen had earlier abducted a businessman who deals in fuel, cement and fertiliser.” He said, “The attackers opened fire on the NSCDC officer after the headlight of his motorcycle exposed their movement as they were fleeing the area with the abducted businessman.” Tabitha said, “The incident has heightened concerns over the security situation in Pushit and surrounding communities despite measures put in place to curb attacks.” He urged security agencies and the Plateau State Government “to urgently strengthen security in Pushit District and ensure the safe release of the abducted businessman.” He said, “Residents are particularly worried by the repeated attacks recorded in communities within the district, including Vodni, Sabon Gari and Nchiya.” Tabitha appealed to residents “to remain vigilant and report suspicious movements to security agencies.” Efforts to reach security operatives for confirmation of the incident as of the time of filing this report were unsuccessful. The post Gunmen kill NSCDC officer, abduct businessman in Plateau appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: UK to deploy fighter jets to help protect Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks
items.description: British fighter planes will be deployed to help Saudi Arabia defend itself against increasing attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels, the UK government announced on Tuesday. The defence ministry said the deployment formed part of “additional defensive military support” to Riyadh. “The UK will fly defensive counter air missions to support the protection of Saudi cities and critical national infrastructure against aerial attack, using RAF Typhoon fighter jets,” the Ministry of Defence (MoD) said in a statement. “These aircraft will operate in a defensive role and will not conduct offensive strikes against the Houthis.” Britain will also deploy a military transport aircraft “to support the movement of defence material within Saudi Arabia alongside UK military advisers to support Saudi staff officers”, the statement added. “The continuing attacks from the Houthis on our ally Saudi Arabia are absolutely despicable,” said Defence Minister Wes Streeting. “The targeting of the airport in Riyadh in particular shows the lengths the Houthis are going to (to) escalate the situation in the region,” he added. The Saudi capital’s international airport has been targeted by strikes 20 times since the beginning of the month, with a recent attack killing 13 people and wounding more than 300. The Houthis have imposed a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia, hitting its tankers, seizing swathes of Yemen’s Red Sea coast vital for oil exports and causing energy prices to jump, while also raining missiles on the kingdom. Yemen’s civil war — in which Saudi Arabia has led a military coalition supporting the government since 2015 — reignited in September after the collapse of a years-long truce. Saudi Arabia, the Yemeni government and the United States accuse Iran of backing the Houthis — an allegation Tehran denies.

items.title: Nii the Menace completes 240km run from Accra to Kumasi to promote breast cancer awareness
items.description: For seven days, Caleb Nii Okai pushed through pain, exhaustion and challenging weather to complete a 240-kilometre run from Accra to Kumasi, carrying a message about breast cancer awareness and the importance of early screening. Popularly known as Nii the Menace, the endurance athlete undertook the challenge to encourage women to pay attention to their breast health and seek medical advice when necessary. Starting from the Balme Library at the University of Ghana, Legon, he made his way towards the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) in Kumasi. But for Nii the Menace, the journey was about more than completing a gruelling physical challenge. “I am really passionate when it comes to mothers and women. If not for them, we wouldn’t be here. I felt breast cancer is serious, and I needed to run for a good cause, promoting breast cancer awareness,” he told David Akuetteh on Luv FM. Over the seven days, Caleb covered an average of 35 to 40 kilometres daily, spending hours on the road as he moved towards Kumasi. Along the route, he interacted with communities and used his journey to spread awareness about breast cancer and the importance of seeking appropriate medical advice. “At least a mother or sister will see my videos and go get screened. I believed through my effort someone will visit the hospital and get screened,” he said. The journey, however, came with significant challenges. Hilly terrain, harsh weather, dangerous roads and periods without drinking water tested his physical strength and mental resilience. “The journey was scary. I was in so much pain as well. The weather wasn’t conducive. At some point, I wasn’t even getting water. Apart from the road being dangerous, it had its own challenges,” he said. There were moments when abandoning the challenge seemed tempting, but he said the purpose behind the run kept him going. “I felt like stopping so many times, but I refused to because I know that there is a mother out there who would want to hear my message,” he said. The Accra-to-Kumasi challenge is one of several endurance runs Caleb has undertaken in recent months, including an earlier journey to Cape Coast. Away from running, he has interests in boxing, finance and economics. His latest challenge comes amid continuing concerns about breast cancer in Ghana, where late diagnosis remains a major public health challenge. For Caleb, the hope is that his seven-day journey will encourage more women to pay attention to their breast health and seek medical care when necessary. The 240-kilometre run may be over, but he hopes its message will travel much further — just like his journey from Ga to Asanteman.

items.title: Christian Council urges gov’t to deploy more military, police to fight galamsey
items.description: The Christian Council of Ghana (CCG) has called on the government to strengthen enforcement of laws against illegal mining, known as galamsey, and deploy more security personnel and resources to protect water bodies and farmlands. The Council’s Chairman, Rev. Enoch Nii Narh Thompson, said addressing the menace required more than public education and dialogue, stressing the need for law enforcement agencies to ensure that existing laws were upheld. Rev. Thompson, who is also the Executive President of the Ghana Baptist Convention, speaking in an interview on October 20, described illegal mining as an environmental and public health issue that should concern the Church. He said the pollution of water sources and the destruction of land made the fight against galamsey a matter of public interest and a responsibility the Church could not ignore. “If the water bodies that the people drink from are polluted, and the soil is poisoned, it is a business of the Church,” he said. Rev. Thompson disclosed that the Christian Council had held several engagements with the government over illegal mining, including meetings with President John Dramani Mahama. He urged policymakers and the relevant authorities to commit more personnel and resources to enforcement operations, particularly through increased involvement of the military, police and specialised agencies. According to him, the government must ensure that the agencies responsible for tackling illegal mining have the capacity to carry out their duties effectively. “The way forward is for policymakers and implementers to use the resources available to them to tackle the issues head-on. The use of the military, the police and specialised agencies must be increased. More people must be engaged to serve in those areas,” he said. The Council chairman further stressed that efforts to engage mining communities should be accompanied by strict enforcement of the law, arguing that dialogue alone would not bring the practice to an end. “Whilst we talk with people, we must also enforce the laws so that the menace could be brought to an end,” he said..

items.title: GoldBod targets zero raw gold exports by 2030 as local refining expands
items.description: The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) is working towards ending Ghana’s export of raw minerals by 2030, as part of efforts to retain more value from the country’s gold resources through local refining and processing. Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi said GoldBod had entered into refining services agreements with two privately owned local refineries, Gold Coast Refinery and Royal Ghana Gold Refinery. The two facilities have cumulatively refined 25 tonnes of ASM gold purchased and exported by GoldBod in 2026, representing about 30 per cent of the 85.4 tonnes exported as of October 20. Delivering a keynote address at the African Minerals Policy Forum – Mining in Motion 2026, Mr Gyamfi said local refining had accelerated significantly since August. He disclosed that 18.7 tonnes of ASM gold had been refined locally since August 1, while 5.4 tonnes out of the 5.7 tonnes purchased by GoldBod in October had undergone local refining. “Under the visionary leadership of H.E. President John Mahama, the GoldBod is fast-changing Ghana’s tragic story of 100% raw mineral export as at the end of 2024, to zero raw mineral export by the end of 2030,” he said. Mr Gyamfi added that the two refineries were working towards obtaining London Bullion Market Association accreditation within three to five years, with regulatory guidance from GoldBod.

items.title: GoldBod exports 85.4 tonnes of small-scale gold worth $11.6bn in 2026 – Sammy Gyamfi
items.description: The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) has aggregated and exported 85.4 tonnes of artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM) gold valued at US$11.6 billion between January 1 and October 20, 2026, Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi has announced. The figure exceeds the 76 tonnes of large-scale gold exports valued at US$11.1 billion recorded over the same period. Speaking at the African Minerals Policy Forum – Mining in Motion 2026, Mr Gyamfi said GoldBod was on course to surpass its 2025 performance, when ASM gold exports reached approximately 104 tonnes, up from 63 tonnes in 2024. He attributed the increase to reforms introduced to formalise the gold trade, strengthen regulation and curb smuggling. “The Ghana Gold Board was thus established by President Mahama as an integrated response to this hydra-headed legacy problem,” he said, explaining that the board had become the sole buyer, seller, exporter and statutory national assayer of gold in Ghana. Mr Gyamfi described the gains as a “production claw back”, saying the reforms had recovered gold that was already being produced but had previously been lost to smuggling and illegal trading. He added that the US$10.8 billion generated by the ASM sector in foreign exchange in 2025 supported foreign exchange market stability, reserve accumulation and the cedi’s appreciation.

items.title: Ato Forson calls for shift in economic policies to secure Ghana’s future
items.description: Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has urged Ghana to move beyond economic stabilisation and pursue policies that address the underlying challenges facing the economy and support long-term growth. He made the call during a New Economy engagement with lecturers and students at the University of Ghana, where he stressed the need for a change in the country’s approach to economic management. According to Dr Forson, Ghana must use the progress made in stabilising the economy as a foundation for securing a more prosperous future. “We have stabilised the present. Now we must secure the future,” he said. He said the country was at a critical stage in its economic development, requiring decisions that would influence opportunities and living standards for future generations. Dr Forson argued that lasting progress would depend on moving away from policies that merely manage recurring economic difficulties towards reforms that address their root causes. “There are moments when a nation must make a clear break with old patterns. There are moments when public policy must stop managing symptoms and start changing structures. This is such a moment for Ghana,” he said. He also stressed the importance of making timely decisions, noting that the country could not afford to remain tied to economic approaches that had held back its progress. “History does not wait for countries that are afraid to decide,” he said. The Finance Minister said Ghana’s next phase of development should prioritise domestic production, the processing of locally produced agricultural goods and minerals, and the creation of more opportunities for businesses and workers.

items.title: Dagbon Regent pledges to sustain late father’s peace and reconciliation efforts
items.description: The Regent of Dagbon, Kampakuya-Naa Yakubu II, has pledged not to compromise the peace and reconciliation process initiated by his late father, Ya-Na Abukari, assuring that he will strengthen the process to safeguard peace in the kingdom. In a speech read on his behalf during a courtesy visit to President Mahama at the Jubilee House, the Regent said his actions will be guided by the constitution developed for the kingdom, which was drafted by representatives from the various traditional areas of Dagbon and approved by the Dagbon Traditional Council. “Everything my father, His Royal Majesty, stood for is my compass. I will carry out his wishes without fear or favour, and I will continue the work he started but could not finish before he was called to eternity,” he said. The Regent said his late father had worked to build relationships across the kingdom and pledged to preserve those efforts while creating opportunities for further reconciliation. “He built bridges. I will make sure those foundations are secure, and I will build more bridges where the opportunity arises. I will not undermine the peace and reconciliation processes he began,” he stated. Kampakuya-Naa Yakubu II also emphasised the importance of strengthening traditional institutions and ensuring that the kingdom’s affairs were conducted in accordance with its established customs and constitutional provisions. He said the constitution was designed to safeguard the peace achieved in Dagbon and would guide the processes leading to the funeral of the late Ya-Naa. “To safeguard the hard-earned peace of Dagbon, my father developed a constitution for the kingdom. It was drafted by representatives from all the traditional areas of Dagbon and approved by the Dagbon Traditional Council. We will live by it,” he said. On the timeline for the funeral, the Regent explained that the constitution provided for his tenure to last 18 months after the passing of the Ya-Naa. He said the funeral committee would work with the Dagbon Traditional Council and the kingmakers to determine when the funeral could be held responsibly within the stipulated period. According to him, details of the arrangements, including the necessary conditions for a smooth and successful funeral, would be communicated to the public as the process progressed. The Regent reiterated his commitment to maintaining the peace in Dagbon, expressing hope that the relationships built through reconciliation would continue to serve the kingdom and the country as a whole.

items.title: NAIMOS steps up anti-galamsey operations in Wassa Amenfi as chiefs pledge support
items.description: The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) has announced plans to deploy more military personnel to the Western Region as it seeks stronger collaboration with traditional authorities and local government officials to combat illegal mining. The Director of Operations at NAIMOS, Colonel K. S. Appiah, disclosed this during separate engagements with the Omanhene of the Wassa Amenfi Traditional Area, Tetrete Okuamoah Sekyim II, and the Municipal Chief Executive (MCE) for Wassa Amenfi, Raymond Nana Ebbah. The visits formed part of the Secretariat’s stakeholder engagement strategy to strengthen local support for anti-galamsey operations. Col. Appiah said traditional authorities had a critical role to play in restoring order and ensuring the success of efforts to curb illegal mining. “The reason why I have decided to engage traditional councils is because of the important role traditional leaders play in establishing order in their areas. Therefore, I do not want to conduct surprise operations which will affect communities without allowing the traditional leaders to ask their subjects to reform,” he said. Col. Appiah said the approach was intended to encourage community leaders and miners to reconsider activities contributing to the destruction of water bodies, forest reserves and the wider environment. He called on the chiefs and the MCE to support efforts to protect state lands and public buildings while promoting responsible mining. “We will deploy our military men to support. I will try everything possible to ensure we mine responsibly. This is what we want — responsible mining,” he said. Paramount chief vows not to shield offenders The Omanhene, Tetrete Okuamoah Sekyim II, welcomed the NAIMOS delegation and pledged the full support of the traditional council. He said illegal mining had destroyed farmlands and water bodies, threatening the future of young people in the area. The paramount chief called for closer cooperation between traditional authorities and the government to end the practice. He assured the Secretariat that the traditional council would not shield any chief or individual involved in illegal mining and would provide credible information to support operations. “We as traditional leaders are ready to support you. This land belongs to us, and we cannot sit down for it to be destroyed. We will give you all the support you need to succeed,” he said. Assembly pledges logistics and intelligence The MCE, Raymond Nana Ebbah, also pledged the Assembly’s support for NAIMOS, saying local authorities were already working with traditional leaders to reclaim degraded lands. He said the Assembly would provide logistical assistance and local intelligence to support the operations. Mr Ebbah stressed that sustainable development in Wassa Amenfi would remain difficult if illegal mining continued to damage the environment. “On behalf of the Assembly and the people of Wassa Amenfi, we welcome you, and we promise to partner with NAIMOS. We will do everything within our power to help you succeed. The President has tasked us to protect our environment, and we will not fail,” he said.

items.title: Rubio says India made 'substantial progress' in diversifying oil purchases
items.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Tuesday that India had made “substantial progress” in diversifying its energy supplies, including away from its key importer, Russia. “What India has expressed repeatedly is their desire to diversify their energy portfolio, which is a smart thing to do,” Rubio said on a visit to India’s economic capital, Mumbai. “Obviously, it’s not easy to do that from one day to the next, so I think they’ve made substantial progress in that regard, and we’re happy to see that.” This is Rubio’s second official visit to the country this year, as he pursues an Asian tour blending diplomacy and trade. He has visited Uzbekistan, where he called for stronger partnerships with Central Asian countries, before landing in Mumbai for talks with Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar and meetings with business leaders. India is a major importer of Russian oil, and US President Donald Trump’s tariff war launched in April last year has added to friction between Washington and New Delhi. “Obviously, we think we could be a source of some of their energy inputs,” Rubio said. The top US diplomat will visit Jamnagar, in the western state of Gujarat, a port and stronghold of billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance conglomerate and its flagship refinery, the world’s largest. “India is a refining superpower,” said Rubio. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi is not scheduled to meet Rubio this time. Washington’s top diplomat is also due to lay a wreath in memory of the 2008 Mumbai attacks that killed 166 people. The top US diplomat visited New Delhi and Kolkata in May this year, while also touring the Taj Mahal and meeting Modi. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Tuesday he had also spoken to Rubio and raised issues with the US military satellite system that Ukraine uses, as well as missile delays. Zelensky, expected in Oslo for talks with US envoys, said he told Rubio that “Starlink/Starshield needs to be restored” and that ballistic missile interceptors “are needed to protect lives”. ‘Energy supplies’ Rubio’s visit comes as India and the United States struggle to finalise a trade deal, a persistent source of friction between the two countries. “We’re very very close; I would say we’re about as close as you can be without having an executed agreement. I think there’s a small number of items left to wrap up,” Rubio said. “Hopefully have some good news to announce fairly soon, and perhaps the leaders can sign it thereafter.” Speaking in Samarkand earlier this week, Rubio said Washington and New Delhi were “very close” to an agreement. However, a deal during his visit appears unlikely. Asked about temporary US sanctions waivers for Russian oil , Rubio said Washington had to juggle multiple factors “including our bilateral relationships with other countries and what they realistically are capable of being able to do in terms of their own energy supplies”. “You also can’t unravel the economy of other countries because of one central issue,” he said. The two countries reached an interim trade agreement in February aimed at reducing US tariffs on Indian goods. But days later, the US Supreme Court struck down Trump’s sweeping tariffs, fuelling uncertainty over when the agreement would take effect. The two sides have been negotiating ever since. Indian Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said this month the talks had reached “a plateau, beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult”. Jaishankar met with his United Arab Emirates counterpart in Mumbai earlier on Tuesday. The UAE is a key supplier of Indian energy, especially liquefied natural gas (LNG). “The situation in the Gulf remains a matter of deep concern,” Jaishankar told UAE Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, in public comments broadcast before their meeting started. He said India continues to support “free, safe and unimpeded flow of trade, energy and fertiliser”.

items.title: Ghana, Burkina Faso explore stronger energy cooperation as SONABHY CEO visits Jinapor
items.description: Ghana and Burkina Faso are exploring ways to deepen cooperation in petroleum transportation and supply following a meeting between the Minister for Energy and Green Transition, Dr John Abdulai Jinapor, and a delegation from Burkina Faso’s national petroleum company, SONABHY. The delegation, led by the newly appointed Chief Executive Officer of Société Nationale Burkinabè d’Hydrocarbures, Forogo Patrice, paid a courtesy call on the minister to discuss ways to strengthen the existing partnership between the two countries. In a Facebook post on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, Dr Jinapor said the discussions focused on improving collaboration in petroleum transportation and supply, deepening regional energy cooperation and advancing shared priorities. The engagement comes as Ghana’s role in facilitating petroleum transit to Burkina Faso continues to grow. Dr Jinapor disclosed that approximately 40% of Burkina Faso’s petroleum products are currently transported through Ghana, compared with 15% two years ago. The SONABHY delegation expressed appreciation to the Government of Ghana for its continued support in facilitating the procurement and transit of petroleum products through the country. It also called for deeper collaboration to strengthen the partnership, reflecting the importance of reliable transportation arrangements to the petroleum supply chain between the two neighbouring countries. Dr Jinapor said the meeting provided an opportunity to explore areas where both countries could work more closely together for their mutual benefit.

items.title: Mahama reaffirms commitment to closing northern infrastructure deficit
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has reaffirmed his commitment to addressing the infrastructure deficit in northern Ghana, describing peace and reliable public infrastructure as the two key drivers of private investment and sustainable job creation for the region’s youth. He made the remarks on Monday, October 19, when a delegation of chiefs from the Dagbon Traditional Area, led by the Regent of Dagbon, Kampakuya Naa Yakubu II, paid him a courtesy call. The President assured the delegation of his administration’s commitment to promoting dialogue, maintaining stability and accelerating development across the northern part of the country. “Our fundamental responsibility as a government is to foster a safe, peaceful, and enabling environment—encouraging dialogue at every turn and ensuring that every single community feels protected and valued,” he said. The visit was to express the gratitude of the chiefs and people of Dagbon to the President and the state for their support during the illness, funeral rites, and burial of the late Overlord, Ya-Na Abukari Mahama II, as well as the peaceful enskinment of the Regent. Reaffirming the government’s respect for traditional authority, President Mahama assured the delegation that his administration would respect the autonomy of traditional institutions and refrain from interfering in chieftaincy affairs. “The peace of Dagbon is priceless, and we must safeguard it deliberately through our words, policies, and shared respect for one another. The government holds the customs, sacred traditions, and institutions of Dagbon in the highest esteem. It will always provide the dignity, space, and institutional support you require to lead your people,” he stated. He also paid tribute to the late Ya-Na Abukari Mahama II, recalling his contribution to peace and reconciliation in Dagbon and describing him as a trusted friend and a visionary leader who restored harmony across the kingdom. He encouraged Kampakuya Naa Yakubu II to build on his late father’s legacy by embracing wisdom, consultation and inclusiveness in his leadership. “Your noble father was a bridge-builder of remarkable vision. You have pledged not only to preserve the bridges he painstakingly built, but to construct new ones during your stewardship. Government stands shoulder-to-shoulder with you on this journey,” he said. On infrastructure development, President Mahama announced plans to improve water supply in parts of northern Ghana through an expansion project financed by the European Union. The project will extend piped water networks to Tamale, Yendi and Damongo, while the Dalong waterworks is expected to receive new heavy-duty pumps that will be fully operational in November to improve water supply in Tamale. The interventions are intended to address persistent water shortages, ease the cost of living and doing business, and create better conditions for agro-industrial development in the region. Speaking on behalf of the delegation, Kampakuya Naa Yakubu II pledged to uphold his late father’s legacy of tolerance and progress. He also expressed the kingdom’s readiness to work with the central government to expand opportunities for young entrepreneurs, preserve peace in local communities, and promote economic development across Dagbon.

items.title: Classement FIFA féminin : les Lionnes de l’Atlas stagnent à la 64e place mondiale
items.description: La sélection marocaine féminine conserve la 64e place du classement mondial de la FIFA, publié mardi 20 octobre 2026. Avec 1 384,71 points, les Lionnes de l’Atlas enregistrent toutefois une baisse par rapport au précédent classement et occupent le quatrième rang africain. Les Lionnes de l’Atlas font du surplace au classement mondial. L’équipe nationale féminine du Maroc reste à la 64e position, selon la dernière mise à jour de la Fédération internationale de football association (FIFA), publiée mardi. Malgré cette stabilité au classement, son total passe de 1 402,24 points en juin à 1 384,71 points en octobre. À l’échelle continentale, le Maroc occupe la quatrième place, derrière le Nigeria, désormais 43e mondial malgré une chute de sept rangs, l’Afrique du Sud, 59e après un recul de deux places, et le Cameroun, qui grimpe à la 52e position après avoir remporté la CAN féminine 2026. Le Ghana complète le top 5 africain en se classant 64e mondial, avec cinq places perdues. Sur la scène internationale, l’Espagne consolide sa première place après ses dernières confrontations face aux États-Unis. Les championnes du monde ont remporté leur première rencontre contre les Américaines avant de concéder un match nul, ce qui leur permet d’accroître leur avance au classement. L’Allemagne, troisième, complète le podium après avoir remporté ses deux matches et se rapproche de la deuxième place. Le top 10 enregistre un seul changement notable avec le retour du Danemark à la 10e position, après une victoire et un match nul au Canada. Les Pays-Bas reculent ainsi au 11e rang. items.title: SSNIT takes pension services to the doorstep of Ghanaians with 2026 Mobile Service Week in Techiman
items.description: The Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) has launched its 2026 Mobile Service Week (MSW) in Techiman, the Bono East Regional capital, with a renewed commitment to bringing pension services closer to members and the general public. The annual initiative, held under the theme “Enhancing Service through Digital Transformation,” was officially launched at the forecourt of Techiman Melcom on Monday, October 19, 2026. The week-long event, running from October 19th to 23rd, will see SSNIT establish 68 temporary service touchpoints at designated locations across the country. A Nationwide Push for Accessibility The Mobile Service Week is designed to make it easier for Ghanaians to access SSNIT services, obtain information, and resolve membership-related concerns without traveling long distances to SSNIT offices. Services being offered at the various touchpoints include: Registration of new members Benefits processing and status verification Renewal of pensioner certificates GhanaCard and SSNIT numbers merger General enquiries and other member services GH¢6.71 Billion Paid in Benefits Delivering the keynote address on behalf of the Deputy Director-General in charge of Finance and Operations, Dr. Bernardette Naa Hoffman, the General Manager of Benefits at SSNIT, Frank Molbila, disclosed that as of September 2026, the Trust had paid a total of GH¢6.71 billion in benefits. “These payments cover monthly pensions, invalidity pensions, survivors’ benefits and emigration benefits,” Mr. Molbila stated. He further highlighted the Trust’s efficiency in pension processing, adding: “SSNIT currently processes and pays pensions within seven working days.” Focus on the Informal Sector A key focus of this year’s Mobile Service Week is encouraging self-employed persons, including traders, artisans, drivers, farmers, and various informal sector workers, to enrol on the SSNIT Scheme, contribute regularly, and secure retirement income when due. The event also seeks to encourage workers to adopt and actively use SSNIT’s digital platforms, including the SSNIT Mobile App, to access services and transact business with the Trust with ease. The initiative underscores SSNIT’s commitment to leveraging digital platforms to improve service delivery, enhance accessibility, and make pension services more convenient for members. Recent Innovations Improving Member Experience The keynote address also drew attention to some of the Trust’s recently introduced initiatives aimed at improving member experience and service delivery. These include: . Co-location – bringing multiple services under one roof for convenience · Member Value Programme (MVP) – offering added benefits to members · Telehealth – providing health support services to members · Virtual Branch – enabling members to access services online Mr. Molbila noted that these initiatives “reflect SSNIT’s continued efforts to improve access to services, expand member support and harness technology to deliver more efficient and convenient pension services.” Dignitaries Graced the Occasion The launch was attended by key dignitaries, including the Bono East Regional Minister, Francis Owusu Antwi, as Special Guest of Honour. The Paramount Chief of Techiman Traditional Area, Oseadeeyo Akumfi Ameyaw IV, was represented by Oheneba Nana Owusu Antwi Boasiako II, Chief of Kenten and the Debehene of Techiman Traditional Area. Oheneba Nana Owusu Antwi Boasiako II officially launched the 2026 SSNIT Mobile Service Week and expressed gratitude to the Trust for its customer-focused approach. “We are grateful to SSNIT for the introduction of its mobile services, which bring its operations to the doorstep of its customers,” he said. In his remarks, the Bono East Regional Minister noted that the initiative is particularly relevant to the people of the region, where agriculture, commerce, and small businesses drive the local economy. “This programme provides important opportunities for pensioners and strengthens retirement benefits for workers and pensioners across the area and the country,” Mr. Owusu Antwi stated. Beneficiaries Share Their Stories The human impact of the SSNIT Scheme was made tangible during the event when three beneficiaries comprising two invalidity pensioners and one survivor beneficiary shared their positive experiences and testified to the Scheme’s impact on their lives. They praised SSNIT for its commitment and swift action in ensuring they receive their pension payments on time. Securing the Future of Every Ghanaian Worker With GH¢6.71 billion paid in benefits, pensions processed within seven working days, and a strong push towards digital transformation, SSNIT is demonstrating that it is not just a pension scheme, but a reliable partner in securing the future of every Ghanaian worker. The 2026 Mobile Service Week is a clear testament to the Trust’s commitment to leaving no one behind, whether in the bustling markets of Techiman or the remote farming communities across the country.

items.title: Futsal : la CAF salue la démonstration du Maroc face à l’Égypte
items.description: Qualifiée pour la finale de la CAN de futsal 2026 après sa large victoire face à l’Égypte (6-0), la sélection marocaine a reçu les éloges de la Confédération africaine de football (CAF). Les Lions de l’Atlas viseront mercredi un quatrième sacre continental consécutif face à l’Angola. La prestation des Lions de l’Atlas du futsal face à l’Égypte n’est pas passée inaperçue. La Confédération africaine de football (CAF) a consacré un article sur son site officiel à la performance de la sélection marocaine, qui s’est qualifiée pour la finale de la Coupe d’Afrique des nations de futsal « Maroc 2026 » grâce à une victoire convaincante sur le score de 6 buts à 0. Disputée lundi soir dans la salle sportive du complexe du prince Moulay Abdellah, à Rabat, cette demi-finale a été largement dominée par les hommes de Hicham Dguig. Selon la CAF, les champions en titre ont imposé leur rythme dès les premières minutes, confirmant leurs ambitions de conserver leur couronne continentale et de décrocher un quatrième titre consécutif. Une domination marquée par six buts Le Maroc a rapidement pris les commandes de la rencontre. Bilal Bakkali a ouvert le score à la 9e minute, avant qu’Ismail Amzal ne double la mise une minute plus tard. Ce dernier a ensuite inscrit son deuxième but personnel à la 15e minute, permettant aux Lions de l’Atlas de rejoindre les vestiaires avec une avance confortable de trois buts. Au retour de la pause, les Marocains ont poursuivi leur domination offensive. Bilal Bakkali a signé un doublé à la 22e minute, portant le score à 4-0. Soufiane Charraoui a ensuite participé à la fête en inscrivant le cinquième but à la 31e minute, avant de clôturer le festival offensif à la 38e minute, lui aussi avec un doublé. Cette victoire nette confirme la solidité de la sélection marocaine, qui poursuit son parcours avec l’objectif de conserver son titre continental à domicile. L’Angola, dernier obstacle vers le sacre En finale, prévue mercredi à 20 heures, heure locale, le Maroc affrontera l’Angola. Cette dernière a décroché son billet après avoir renversé l’Algérie (3-2), alors qu’elle était menée de deux buts. Avant cette affiche, l’Égypte et l’Algérie se disputeront la troisième place du tournoi à partir de 17 heures. Portés par leur public et forts de leur démonstration en demi-finale, les Lions de l’Atlas auront désormais l’occasion de confirmer leur domination sur le futsal africain en visant un quatrième titre continental consécutif. items.title: National Apprenticeship Programme pledges business support for Ask Media Training School graduates
items.description: The National Apprenticeship Programme has pledged to support graduates of Ask Media Training School with tools to establish their own businesses, urging them to turn their practical skills into sustainable livelihoods. National Deputy Coordinator of the programme, Fouad Agbenyadzi, says graduates could approach the National Youth Authority, where the programme operates, to explore available support. The ceremony was held under the theme, “Empowering Creative Features through Practical Excellence,” highlighting the importance of practical training, entrepreneurship and skills development in preparing young people for the world of work. Speaking at the Institute’s 2026 graduation ceremony at the Great Hall of the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), he said the initiative was committed to helping young people apply their skills to business development. “What we can also do to support them is to support them with the needed tools that will assist them to do their business,” he said. Mr Agbenyadzi explained that the programme connects aspiring apprentices with Master Craft Persons and pays their training fees to equip them with practical skills. He added that the support extended to different trades, including media and videography, as part of efforts to improve youth employment. “As far as practical training, media, videography, whatever, as far as it’s a trade that you have gone through, we will assist them,” he noted. The Chief Executive Officer of Ask Media Training Institute, Amankwaa Agyeman, challenged the graduates to become job creators rather than depend solely on government employment. “We cannot all wait for government jobs. We must become job creators, problem solvers, and innovators,” he said. He disclosed that the institute has trained more than 6,545 media professionals. Mr Agyeman also recounted the challenges of building the institution, including two fires that destroyed investments within three years and the need to relocate after more than a decade at its former premises. “You can lose buildings without losing your vision, encouraging the graduates to remain determined despite setbacks,” he added. Drawing on these experiences, he officially launched his book, ‘Entrepreneurship Is Crazy, but it’s the Best Decision’, which explores the challenges and rewards of entrepreneurship. “Entrepreneurship is exciting. Entrepreneurship is rewarding. But let me be honest with you, entrepreneurship is also crazy,” he indicated. He urged the graduates to start small, apply their skills, and remain committed to continuous learning. One of the graduates, Asumadu Benjamin Willberforce, who trained in sports presentation, expressed excitement about completing the programme and optimism about his future in the media industry. “I am very excited for graduating today. Not everybody would have got this opportunity to be a graduate,” he noted. He acknowledged that developing his presentation skills had been challenging but said consistency and determination had helped him improve. Mr Willberforce also urged graduates to take the initiative in seeking employment rather than wait for opportunities to come to them. “You don’t need to sit down for someone to call you that there has been a job opportunity. You need to go through by yourself,” he added.

items.title: Feijóo propone exigir a los nacionalizados un “tiempo de residencia mínima” en España para poder votar
items.description: La conocida como ley de nietos promovida por el Gobierno de Pedro Sánchez y la correspondiente suspensión cautelar del Tribunal Supremo del derecho al voto para quienes hayan sido nacionalizados a través de esta vía han llevado a Génova a estudiar una propuesta normativa sin precedentes. El Partido Popular ya había anunciado que, si Alberto Núñez Feijóo es investido presidente tras el 29-N, el PP impulsará una nueva ley de nacionalidad que endurezca los requisitos para obtener el pasaporte español. Pero el líder del PP no se ha quedado ahí y este martes ha propuesto además exigir, para poder votar en las elecciones, a quienes hayan sido nacionalizados un “tiempo de residencia mínima” en el país. “Una cosa es tener un pasaporte y otra cosa es tener derecho a voto”, ha sentenciado Feijóo este martes en una entrevista en la Cadena Cope. items.title: El Mansouri fixe des objectifs de croissance et mise sur l’eau, les énergies et la souveraineté alimentaire
items.description: La cheffe du gouvernement, Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, a présenté lundi devant les deux Chambres du Parlement les grandes orientations du programme gouvernemental pour la période 2027/31. Le document fixe notamment un objectif de croissance annuelle moyenne de 5 %, une réduction de l’endettement à près de 62 % à l’horizon 2031, ainsi que des engagements en matière de sécurité hydrique, énergétique, alimentaire et numérique. Le gouvernement entend adopter une trajectoire économique qu’il présente comme volontariste et réaliste. Lors de la présentation du programme gouvernemental, lundi 19 octobre, Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri a annoncé un objectif de croissance annuelle moyenne de 5 % sur la période 2027-2031. L’Exécutif prévoit également de contenir l’inflation à 2 % par an afin de préserver le pouvoir d’achat et la stabilité, tout en limitant le déficit budgétaire à 3 % du produit intérieur brut (PIB) sur la période 2026-2031. Pour atteindre ces objectifs, la cheffe du gouvernement a évoqué l’élargissement de l’assiette fiscale, l’amélioration de l’efficacité des dépenses dans le cadre de la réforme de la loi organique relative à la loi de finances, la mobilisation des effets de la croissance et l’augmentation de la contribution des établissements et entreprises publics. Le gouvernement prévoit aussi d’inscrire la dette dans une trajectoire descendante, pour la ramener à près de 62 % à l’horizon 2031. Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri a souligné que la mise en œuvre du programme relève de la responsabilité du gouvernement, sous le contrôle et l’évaluation du Parlement, avec la contribution des forces nationales et des médias. Elle a également affirmé que l’Exécutif entend rester au service de l’ensemble des Marocains, quelles que soient leurs catégories sociales et leurs orientations politiques, et maintenir le dialogue avec la majorité, l’opposition, les partenaires sociaux et économiques, la société civile, les acteurs des droits humains et les médias. Sécurité hydrique : 1,8 milliard m3 d’eau dessalée à l’horizon 2031 La sécurité hydrique figure parmi les axes annoncés du programme. La cheffe du gouvernement a indiqué que l’Exécutif entend accélérer la réalisation des stations de dessalement de l’eau de mer afin de mobiliser 1,8 milliard de mètres cubes d’eau à l’horizon 2031. La stratégie prévoit également de diversifier et de renforcer l’offre en eau, notamment par l’accélération de la construction de barrages, en particulier dans les régions arides et semi-arides, les zones montagneuses et les oasis. Des projets de transfert d’eau entre bassins et régions sont aussi prévus lorsque cela s’avère nécessaire, sans porter atteinte aux équilibres hydriques des territoires concernés. Pour assurer la durabilité de la sécurité hydrique, le gouvernement s’engage à élaborer un plan national de l’eau destiné à servir de cadre stratégique à long terme. Celui-ci devra tenir compte des spécificités naturelles, climatiques, économiques et sociales du pays et assurer la convergence des politiques publiques relatives à l’eau, à l’agriculture, à l’énergie, à l’environnement et à l’aménagement du territoire. Plus de 52% du mix énergétique en 2030 Sur le volet énergétique, Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri a annoncé l’accélération du programme de développement des énergies renouvelables, avec l’objectif de porter leur part à plus de 52 % du mix énergétique à l’horizon 2030. Le gouvernement prévoit également de mettre en œuvre l’offre du Maroc en matière d’hydrogène vert et de déployer progressivement la feuille de route relative aux infrastructures gazières. En parallèle, il entend rationaliser la demande croissante en énergie grâce à des mesures d’efficacité énergétique. Porter la part des semences nationales à 50% En matière de sécurité alimentaire, la cheffe du gouvernement a annoncé une orientation visant à passer d’un soutien conjoncturel à une meilleure maîtrise des facteurs de production. Un programme consacré à la souveraineté en matière de semences doit permettre de faire passer la part des semences nationales de 20 % à 50 % au cours du mandat. Le gouvernement prévoit aussi de sécuriser les stocks et l’approvisionnement du marché, de réviser les réserves de céréales et de réguler les exportations des filières sensibles. La reconstitution du cheptel figure également parmi les engagements annoncés. Elle doit notamment passer par la facilitation de l’accès des petits éleveurs aux races à forte productivité, le soutien aux races locales ainsi que le renforcement de la vigilance sanitaire et épidémiologique. Cybersécurité et protection des données Le programme gouvernemental prévoit la mise en place d’un mécanisme national intégré consacré à la cybersécurité et à la protection des données et des systèmes vitaux. L’Exécutif entend également étendre l’accès à Internet, particulièrement dans les zones éloignées, élaborer un cadre pour une intelligence artificielle sûre et responsable, attirer les investissements et soutenir les start-up innovantes. Renforcer les chaînes de valeur La cheffe du gouvernement a aussi mis l’accent sur le renforcement de la souveraineté industrielle et de la place du Maroc dans les chaînes de valeur. Cette orientation doit notamment s’appuyer sur la mise en œuvre des initiatives royales africaines et atlantiques, ainsi que sur le développement des corridors maritimes, logistiques et énergétiques, des nouveaux métiers et des industries à faible empreinte carbone. « En application des Hautes Orientations royales, nous réunirons les conditions nécessaires à l’émergence d’une base industrielle et technologique de défense, en améliorant le cadre juridique, la compétitivité et les incitations », a déclaré Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri. Elle a également annoncé la volonté de constituer une flotte nationale de marine marchande forte et compétitive, tout en accélérant les grands projets portuaires et les zones logistiques et industrielles qui leur sont associées. Pour la cheffe du gouvernement, les transformations mondiales imposent une approche intégrant la sécurité hydrique, alimentaire, énergétique et environnementale, ainsi que les risques géostratégiques et les nouveaux risques numériques et scientifiques. items.title: PM Shehbaz ready to build consensus on counterterrorism if opposition willing to: Sanaullah
items.description: Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah on Tuesday said the federal government was ready to invite all political parties and build consensus on counterterrorism. Speaking in the Senate, the PML-N leader also urged the opposition to “set other demands aside”. The PM’s aide’s remarks come after the Centre imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on October 11, citing the PTI-led provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The decisions were also endorsed by the Parliament last week amid protests by the opposition. “Even now, if all parties [..] can agree to sit down to discuss this issue, then Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif is willing to invite them and find a way forward (on counterterrorism) or how operations can be supported by the entire nation,” Sanaullah said, urging political parties to put other demands aside and “stand united” in tackling terrorism. Sanaullah went on to criticise National Assembly Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai. “He became the leader of the opposition after the speaker signed off on his appointment; however, [..] he does not accept the speaker’s authority and is not even ready to meet the prime minister and has even refused to sit in the speaker’s chambers with the PM,” Sanaullah said. Sanaullah then turned his attention to the rise in terrorism in the country, expressing sorrow at the martyrdom of an army officer a day earlier. Addressing the opposition, he said, “You are running propaganda against the head of this institution and [..] making below-the-belt remarks.” The PML-N senator also assailed the members of the now non-functional PTI-led KP government for not attending apex committee meetings. “In 11 months, there was one apex committee meeting in which the KP CM was in attendance, and the way he was brought there, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi already spoke about it,” Sanaullah said. Recalling the federal government’s talks with the PTI earlier this month, Sanaullah said: “During the talks, we agreed on constituting a political committee comprising members from both sides; however, [..] the talks broke down on one single point — the PTI fulfilling its responsibilities and supporting the federal government in counterterrorism efforts.” Chaudhry reiterates invitation to opposition Federal Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry also invited opposition parties to develop a consensus against terrorism, saying Pakistan’s peace and the future of its children depended on a united stance against the menace. “I extended an invitation yesterday, and today I am once again inviting all opposition parties to come forward and build a consensus against terrorism,” he said while speaking to the media. “Why can we not develop a consensus, at least on this issue?” he asked. Chaudhry said political differences should not be allowed to compromise the national interest, adding that peace and prosperity required a collective effort. The minister said controlling terrorism in KP was practically impossible without the provincial government’s full cooperation with federal institutions, the Pakistan Army and security agencies. He said the provincial government had refused to cooperate with the federal government on its Afghanistan policy, particularly efforts to prevent cross-border infiltration. “This was the only reason why the emergency was imposed,” he said, referring to the decision concerning the administration of KP. Criticising the PTI, Chaudhry regretted that the party was not prepared to condemn terrorism. “One is that we have to rid Pakistan of terrorism once and for all, and the second is the position of your party, which was in power in KP. The PTI is not even prepared to condemn terrorism,” he said. He said networks linked to terrorists, smuggling operations and influential people patronising them had contributed to the persistence of terrorism in the province. However, Chaudhry said the provincial government was now extending full cooperation and expressed hope that results would become visible soon. He added that counterterrorism operations would continue until the menace was eliminated. Rejecting the impression that the federal government’s move concerning KP was driven by a power struggle, he said the objective was to restore peace. “This is not a power game; it is a peace game,” he said, adding that advisory councils comprising tribal elders had been established in 12 districts to empower local communities and facilitate intelligence-based operations in consultation with them. Drawing a comparison with Balochistan, Chaudhry said the provincial administration and Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti were working alongside law enforcement agencies and federal institutions to combat terrorism. He added that the Balochistan government had not refused to cooperate with the federal government, adding that this was the difference between the two provinces. In the days preceding the imposition of governor’s rule in KP, political tensions between the Centre and the opposition — including the PTI, which was in power in KP — had remained high since jailed former prime minister Imran Khan’s party announced a protest march to Islamabad to demand his release. Intense negotiations between the two sides a week before the imposition of governor’s rule had failed to yield any results, with counterterrorism policy being one of the main reasons behind the breakdown of their talks. The PTI said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre denied . It also called for reviewing the counterterrorism policy, while the latter criticised the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objected to its stance on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban. Soon after, the Centre also authorised the deployment of Pakistan Army troops and assets in aid of civil power in KP. Federal ministers have also alleged that the PTI-led government in KP had a “nexus” with terrorist groups, stating that the province’s security situation necessitated the imposition of emergency there.
